A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2World study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original cart-pole, procedural-maze, and ProcTHOR experiments. Appendix C includes original memory-state, predictive-coding, and failure-case analyses.

after.justification: Retains those original experiments and appendix analyses, adding best-matching-error and context-shuffling results in Figures 3 and 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix B retain the same observation encoders/decoders, gated slot attention, training objectives, image-pretraining procedure, and recurrent inference. Renaming ICEL/ICER to EL/ER does not change the method.

E1.justification: Random cart-poles, procedural mazes, and ProcTHOR remain the evaluated domains. v2 adds a corrupted-context maze scenario that shuffles observations while preserving actions, changing evaluation input conditions without introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Dreamer and NWM retain the same comparator memberships in Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6. The new diagnostics examine existing L2World training variants; best-matching error serves as a theoretical diagnostic reference.

E3.justification: The new cart-pole diagnostic evaluates 130 unseen environments at T > 100 and estimates best-matching error using ground-truth training-environment dynamics. The new maze protocol shuffles 20% or 50% of context observations with actions fixed. Existing benchmark splits, training settings, and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Adds two targeted analyses: whether asymptotic cart-pole errors track best-matching error, and whether EL and ER differ in sensitivity to context shuffling. Existing diversity, context-length, over-training, mapping, predictive-coding, and failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing error bars, including those in Figure 2 and the predictive-coding plots, are retained. v2 adds no empirical seed or repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Figure 3 reports increasing departure below best-matching error with greater training-environment coverage. Figure 5 adds shuffling results: at T=1000, 50% shuffling reduces Maze-32K-L PSNR from 24.62 to 19.43, versus 22.05 to 20.44 for Maze-128-L. Existing benchmark values in Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes the ER bound from min{recognition term + best-matching error, worst-matching error} to min{recognition term, training-environment TV diameter} + best-matching error. Appendix A adds Equation (9) and the corresponding proof step. The EL bound, assumptions, and context-length scaling remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain ER/EL formalization and error bounds, L2World, and empirical evidence linking environment diversity and long context to adaptation. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain their substantive scope despite terminology and framing edits.

C2.justification: v1 attributes ProcTHOR's long-context decline to failure to incentivize longer contexts; v2 describes impairment of long-context ability acquired on mazes. v2 also interprets the new diagnostics as evidence of an ER-to-EL transition and EL's greater context dependence. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility Statement adds a direct source-code pointer for the random-cart-pole environment. Existing training-code and maze links, architecture specifications, hardware, optimizer, and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Adds Garg et al., Panwar et al., and 2025 work by Park, Nguyen and Reddy, Wurgaft, and Singh and colleagues. The introduction and related work expand connections to Bayesian ICL, retrieval versus inference, and learning-strategy dynamics without fundamentally changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: Standardizes ICEL/ICER terminology to EL/ER and revises selected introduction, related-work, and interpretation passages. Adds ethics and reproducibility statements and Appendix D on LLM use, alongside affiliation and publication-status updates. The main section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Adds Figures 3 and 5 and moves v1's qualitative Figure 4 into Appendix C as Figure 12. Retained appendix figures are rearranged, table emphasis and scientific notation are adjusted, and the document adopts ICLR formatting. Existing visual evidence is largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The new best-matching-error and context-shuffling diagnostics provide useful additional support for the central ER/EL distinction. The explicit diversity term and added Appendix A derivation clarify the theoretical argument, while updated positioning and benchmark access information improve documentation. These are incremental gains; the core method, benchmark results, and stated limitations remain essentially unchanged.
